course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Revolutions
unit.description: Study how Enlightenment ideas fueled political revolutions and nationalism, and how industrialization transformed economies, governments, and societies.

topic.title: Economic Developments and Innovations in the Industrial Age
topic.summary: How laissez-faire ideas, limited liability, stock markets, and transnational businesses changed economies.

framework.name: InSPECT
framework.title: Use InSPECT to choose your evidence
framework.intro: A fact can connect to more than one lens. Choose the lens that helps answer the prompt.
framework.sourceNote: Based on the class Early Religions + InSPECT slides, pages 5-17.

themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment
themes.question: How did geography, crops, resources, or disease shape choices?
themes.example: Andean terraces made steep slopes more usable for farming.

themes.title: Social interactions and organization
themes.question: Who had status, opportunities, or obligations?
themes.example: Examination preparation favored families that could afford education.

themes.title: Political systems and governance
themes.question: How did rulers gain authority and administer territory?
themes.example: Song officials carried imperial decisions into local government.

themes.title: Economic systems
themes.question: How were goods produced, exchanged, taxed, or distributed?
themes.example: Mali drew revenue from commerce through its territory.

themes.title: Cultural developments and interactions
themes.question: How did beliefs, learning, and artistic practices influence society?
themes.example: Buddhist monasteries connected religious practice with education.

themes.title: Technology and innovation
themes.question: What techniques or tools changed what people could do?
themes.example: Inca roads and knotted records helped officials coordinate resources.

questions.prompt: Supporters of laissez-faire capitalism argued that
choices: markets work best with little government interference
states should accumulate gold through trade surpluses
markets work best when governments set all prices
questions.explanation: Laissez-faire supporters wanted minimal government interference.
choiceExplanations: Laissez-faire supporters wanted minimal government interference.
questions.distinguisher: Accumulating gold through surpluses is mercantilism, which laissez-faire thinkers criticized.

questions.prompt: Limited liability encouraged investment because it
choices: required governments to own half of every company
limited investors' profits to a fixed amount set by the government
limited investors' losses to the money they put in
guaranteed a profit for every investor
questions.explanation: Investors could not lose more than their investment, so risk fell.
choiceExplanations: Investors could not lose more than their investment, so risk fell.
questions.distinguisher: Limited liability capped losses, not profits.

questions.prompt: The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation is an example of
choices: a transnational business founded by Dutch merchants in the 1600s
a transnational business of the industrial age
a state bank of the Qing dynasty
questions.explanation: Founded in 1865, it financed trade across borders in Asia.
choiceExplanations: Founded in 1865, it financed trade across borders in Asia.
questions.distinguisher: It was transnational, but it was founded in 1865.

questions.prompt: Laissez-faire ideas differed from mercantilism in that laissez-faire
questions.explanation: Laissez-faire thinkers opposed the controls mercantilists favored.
choiceExplanations: Supporting trade surpluses and colonies is the mercantilist position.
Government control of trade is what mercantilists favored.
Laissez-faire thinkers opposed the controls mercantilists favored.
questions.distinguisher: Government control of trade is mercantilism.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would best challenge the claim that industrial economies followed pure laissez-faire?
choices: Stock exchanges grew in many countries
Governments built railroads and passed tariffs
Adam Smith wrote in favor of free markets
questions.explanation: State railroads and tariffs show government involvement.
choiceExplanations: State railroads and tariffs show government involvement.
Smith's writing shows the idea, not the practice.
questions.distinguisher: Smith's writing shows the idea existed, not whether economies followed it.

questions.prompt: Smith uses the example of pin-making to illustrate
questions.explanation: He shows one task divided into about eighteen operations.
choiceExplanations: He shows one task divided into about eighteen operations.
questions.distinguisher: Smith describes hand operations, not steam engines.

stimulusBlocks.attribution: Adam Smith, Scottish philosopher and economist, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, 1776
stimulusBlocks.citation: Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, Book I, ch. 1. Project Gutenberg eBook #3300.
stimulusBlocks.note: A manufactory is a workshop. Smith is describing the division of labor in pin-making.
stimulusBlocks.text: One man draws out the wire; another straights it; a third cuts it; a fourth points it; a fifth grinds it at the top for receiving the head; to make the head requires two or three distinct operations; to put it on is a peculiar business; to whiten the pins is another; it is even a trade by itself to put them into the paper; and the important business of making a pin is, in this manner, divided into about eighteen distinct operations, which, in some manufactories, are all performed by distinct hands, though in others the same man will sometimes perform two or three of them. I have seen a small manufactory of this kind, where ten men only were employed, and where some of them consequently performed two or three distinct operations.

questions.prompt: Smith's description is best understood in the context of
choices: factory production powered by electricity and assembly lines
workshop production before the spread of factory machinery
questions.explanation: Smith wrote in 1776, as workshops divided tasks before machines spread.
choiceExplanations: Smith wrote in 1776, as workshops divided tasks before machines spread.
questions.distinguisher: Electric power came more than a century later.

questions.prompt: The process Smith describes most directly contributed to
choices: the end of manufacturing in Britain
questions.explanation: Splitting tasks raised the output each worker could produce.
choiceExplanations: Splitting tasks raised the output each worker could produce.
questions.distinguisher: Specialization lowered costs, so prices tended to fall.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, limited liability encouraged investment because
choices: investors could lose only the money they had put in
investors could lose all of their property, including their homes
questions.explanation: Losses were limited to the investment.
choiceExplanations: Losses were limited to the investment.
questions.distinguisher: Limited liability protected investors' other property.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 5.7 key concept: as the influence of the industrial states grew, new financial instruments and transnational businesses developed, along with laissez-faire capitalism
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing new business organizations, 1850–1900
stimulusBlocks.text:
Laws allowing limited liability, passed in Britain in 1855 and in other countries soon after, meant that investors could lose only the money they had put into a company. This encouraged many people to buy stocks, and stock exchanges grew. Large banks and companies began to operate across borders. The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation, founded in 1865, financed trade across Asia.

Supporters of laissez-faire capitalism argued that markets worked best with little government interference. Critics pointed to monopolies, harsh working conditions, and periodic economic crises.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, critics of laissez-faire capitalism pointed to
choices: monopolies, harsh working conditions, and crises
questions.explanation: The passage names monopolies, conditions, and crises.
choiceExplanations: The passage names monopolies, conditions, and crises.
questions.distinguisher: Critics wanted more regulation, not less.

questions.prompt: The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation is best understood in the context of
choices: the closing of Asian ports to trade
growing global trade linked to industrial economies
questions.explanation: It financed expanding trade between Asia and industrial economies.
choiceExplanations: The Mongol Empire was much earlier.
It financed expanding trade between Asia and industrial economies.
questions.distinguisher: Asian trade was expanding, not closing.
